purpose: Tracked, authenticated pins for every scanner binary the supply-chain gate executes. A scan from an unverified binary is not evidence: the finding set is version-dependent, and an unauthenticated download is an unverified input to the gate that is supposed to verify inputs.
provenance: Every sha256 below is the value published in the upstream project's own release checksums file for that exact release tag, recorded here verbatim so CI can authenticate the download offline against tracked source rather than trusting the transport.

vulnerability_database.note: trivy 0.73.0 records an OCI digest for the checks bundle but NOT for the vulnerability database, so the vuln DB is bound by the byte digest of its cache artifacts instead. That limitation is upstream and is recorded rather than papered over.

executed_binary_authentication.$comment: A --version string is a claim a binary makes about itself, so it is not authentication. The installer verifies the release ARCHIVE digest and then the EXTRACTED EXECUTABLE digest; the runner independently re-verifies the bytes of the executable it actually resolves on PATH and refuses to scan on any mismatch. A different binary that reports the correct version is therefore still rejected.
executed_binary_authentication.note: These executable digests are the upstream RELEASE builds. Distribution rebuilds (for example Homebrew) produce different bytes for the same version and are correctly rejected: install via scripts/gate/install-scanners.sh so the gate runs the exact audited artifacts.
